_why: Names that mean nothing to a reader outside this workspace, and must not reach a repository the public can read. Checked by scripts/check-naming.mjs on every pipeline. A rule is data, not code: add one here rather than editing the script. Each rule declares a scope - "files", "messages", or both; omitted means both. Three ways out, narrowest first: naming-gate:allow <rule-id> - <reason> on a single line; a rule’s own `exclude` for a class of file it cannot speak to; and exemptPaths below for a file that is ABOUT the rules and would otherwise have to fight them on every edit.

rules.message: An unannounced product name. Say what the thing is: "an OpenRS discovery front end", "the discovery UI" - which is what the code already calls it in VITE_DISCOVERY_ACTIVE and isDiscoveryActive.
A section number from a planning document that lives in the workspace and ships to nobody. Say what it means - in every case measured here, the sentence around it already did.
rules._exclude_why: The .graphqls files are copied from dcb-service and re-taken whenever that contract moves. Editing their comments here is drift that the next copy silently reverts; the fix belongs upstream.
rules._scope_why: Files only. The doctrine names the commit message as one of the three places a plan’s section numbers are allowed to live, so failing on one there would contradict the rule this gate enforces.

rules.message: A workspace planning document. It is not in this repository and never will be, so a reader cannot follow the pointer. Put the argument in docs/ or the commit message.
rules._measured: Zero matches when this rule was added on 2026-09-24. It is here because the workspace plans are where the other two rules’ names come from, so this is the path by which the next one arrives.
rules._scope_why: Files only, for the same reason as plan-reference.

exemptPaths.why: The rules themselves. Every pattern is a literal example of what it forbids.
The checker. It holds no names today - they are all data - but it is where one would land next.
The documentation of these rules, which cannot explain what they catch without quoting it.
Generated, and not prose any reader reads.
